claim: TRPM3 channels are activated by heat.
source: Transient receptor potential melastatin 3 (TRPM3) channels are activated by heat (Vriens et al., 2011), and a number of chemical ligands such as pregnenolone sulphate (PregS) (Oberwinkler and Philipp, 2014) and the newly described synthetic agonist CIM0216 (Held et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Vriens et al., 2011.

claim: TRPM3 channels are activated by pregnenolone sulphate (PregS).
source: Transient receptor potential melastatin 3 (TRPM3) channels are activated by heat (Vriens et al., 2011), and a number of chemical ligands such as pregnenolone sulphate (PregS) (Oberwinkler and Philipp, 2014) and the newly described synthetic agonist CIM0216 (Held et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Oberwinkler and Philipp, 2014.

claim: TRPM3 channels are activated by the synthetic agonist CIM0216.
source: Transient receptor potential melastatin 3 (TRPM3) channels are activated by heat (Vriens et al., 2011), and a number of chemical ligands such as pregnenolone sulphate (PregS) (Oberwinkler and Philipp, 2014) and the newly described synthetic agonist CIM0216 (Held et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Held et al., 2015.

claim: Activation of receptors coupled to heterotrimeric Gi/o proteins inhibits TRPM3 channels.
source: Here, we show that activation of receptors coupled to heterotrimeric Gi/o proteins inhibits TRPM3 channels.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by multiple experimental approaches including whole-cell patch clamp, Ca2+ imaging, and behavioral experiments shown throughout the manuscript.

claim: Inhibition of TRPM3 by Gi/o-coupled receptors was alleviated by co-expression of proteins that bind Gβγ subunits.
source: This inhibition was alleviated by co-expression of proteins that bind the βγ subunits of heterotrimeric G-proteins (Gβγ).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1, where co-expression of βARK-CT (a Gβγ sink) attenuated inhibition.

claim: Co-expression of Gβγ inhibited TRPM3 currents.
source: Co-expression of Gβγ, but not constitutively active Gαi or Gαo, inhibited TRPM3 currents.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2, where co-expression of Gβ1γ2 significantly inhibited TRPM3 currents in Xenopus oocytes.

claim: Constitutively active Gαi does not inhibit TRPM3 currents.
source: Co-expression of Gβγ, but not constitutively active Gαi or Gαo, inhibited TRPM3 currents.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D, where constitutively active Gαi2 did not inhibit TRPM3 activity.

claim: Constitutively active Gαo does not inhibit TRPM3 currents.
source: Co-expression of Gβγ, but not constitutively active Gαi or Gαo, inhibited TRPM3 currents.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D, where constitutively active Gαo did not inhibit TRPM3 activity.

claim: TRPM3 co-immunoprecipitated with Gβ.
source: TRPM3 co-immunoprecipitated with Gβ, and purified Gβγ proteins applied to excised inside-out patches inhibited TRPM3 currents, indicating a direct effect.
evidence: This claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Purified Gβγ proteins applied to excised inside-out patches inhibited TRPM3 currents.
source: TRPM3 co-immunoprecipitated with Gβ, and purified Gβγ proteins applied to excised inside-out patches inhibited TRPM3 currents, indicating a direct effect.
evidence: This claim is supported by excised patch clamp experiments shown in Figure 3A-D.

claim: Gβγ inhibits TRPM3 via a direct effect.
source: TRPM3 co-immunoprecipitated with Gβ, and purified Gβγ proteins applied to excised inside-out patches inhibited TRPM3 currents, indicating a direct effect.
evidence: This is inferred from the combination of co-immunoprecipitation data and the effect of purified Gβγ on excised patches.

claim: Baclofen inhibited Ca2+ signals induced by PregS in mouse dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons.
source: Baclofen and somatostatin, agonists of Gi-coupled receptors, inhibited Ca2+ signals induced by PregS and CIM0216 in mouse dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons.
evidence: This claim is supported by Ca2+ imaging experiments shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Somatostatin inhibited Ca2+ signals induced by PregS in mouse dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons.
source: Baclofen and somatostatin, agonists of Gi-coupled receptors, inhibited Ca2+ signals induced by PregS and CIM0216 in mouse dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons.
evidence: This claim is supported by Ca2+ imaging experiments shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Baclofen inhibited Ca2+ signals induced by CIM0216 in mouse dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons.
source: Baclofen and somatostatin, agonists of Gi-coupled receptors, inhibited Ca2+ signals induced by PregS and CIM0216 in mouse dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons.
evidence: This claim is supported by Ca2+ imaging experiments shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Somatostatin inhibited Ca2+ signals induced by CIM0216 in mouse dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons.
source: Baclofen and somatostatin, agonists of Gi-coupled receptors, inhibited Ca2+ signals induced by PregS and CIM0216 in mouse dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and is consistent with the experimental approach, though the specific CIM0216 + somatostatin data is not shown in detail.

claim: The GABAB receptor agonist baclofen inhibited inward currents induced by CIM0216 in DRG neurons.
source: The GABAB receptor agonist baclofen also inhibited inward currents induced by CIM0216 in DRG neurons, and nocifensive responses elicited by this TRPM3 agonist in mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by whole-cell patch clamp experiments shown in Figure 6.

claim: Baclofen inhibited nocifensive responses elicited by CIM0216 in mice.
source: The GABAB receptor agonist baclofen also inhibited inward currents induced by CIM0216 in DRG neurons, and nocifensive responses elicited by this TRPM3 agonist in mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral experiments shown in Figure 7A-B.

claim: TRPM3 channels act as heat sensors in dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons.
source: These channels were shown to act as heat sensors in dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons; mice lacking TRPM3 had altered behavioral responses to noxious heat (Vriens et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Vriens et al., 2011.

claim: Mice lacking TRPM3 had altered behavioral responses to noxious heat.
source: These channels were shown to act as heat sensors in dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons; mice lacking TRPM3 had altered behavioral responses to noxious heat (Vriens et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Vriens et al., 2011.

claim: TRPM3 is expressed in the brain.
source: TRPM3 is also expressed in a variety of other tissues, including the brain, kidneys and pancreatic β-cells (Oberwinkler and Philipp, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Oberwinkler and Philipp, 2014.

claim: TRPM3 is expressed in the kidneys.
source: TRPM3 is also expressed in a variety of other tissues, including the brain, kidneys and pancreatic β-cells (Oberwinkler and Philipp, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Oberwinkler and Philipp, 2014.

claim: TRPM3 is expressed in pancreatic β-cells.
source: TRPM3 is also expressed in a variety of other tissues, including the brain, kidneys and pancreatic β-cells (Oberwinkler and Philipp, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Oberwinkler and Philipp, 2014.

claim: Gβγ subunits were originally thought to be scaffolds for the Gα subunits, keeping them inactive in non-stimulated cells.
source: The βγ subunits of heterotrimeric G-proteins were originally thought to be scaffolds for the Gα subunits, keeping them inactive in non-stimulated cells.
evidence: This is a statement about the historical understanding of Gβγ function, representing established scientific knowledge.

claim: Seminal work on cardiac G-protein activated K+ (GIRK) channels demonstrated important direct physiological roles for Gβγ.
source: Seminal work on cardiac G-protein activated K+ (GIRK) channels demonstrated important direct physiological roles for Gβγ (Logothetis et al., 1987).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Logothetis et al., 1987.

claim: All GIRK channels (Kir3.1–3.4) are activated by cell surface receptors that couple to heterotrimeric Gi/o proteins, via direct binding of Gβγ to the channel.
source: All GIRK channels (Kir3.1–3.4) are activated by cell surface receptors that couple to heterotrimeric Gi/o proteins, via direct binding of Gβγ to the channel.
evidence: This is established knowledge about GIRK channel regulation.

claim: GIRK channel activation by Gβγ plays roles in slowing the heart rate by muscarinic stimulation.
source: This effect plays roles in slowing the heart rate by muscarinic stimulation, and in the analgesic effects of opioids (Hibino et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Hibino et al., 2010.

claim: GIRK channel activation by Gβγ plays roles in the analgesic effects of opioids.
source: This effect plays roles in slowing the heart rate by muscarinic stimulation, and in the analgesic effects of opioids (Hibino et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Hibino et al., 2010.

claim: PregS-induced TRPM3 activity requires the presence of the membrane phospholipid phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate [PI(4,5)P2].
source: We and others have shown recently that in various cellular expression systems PregS-induced TRPM3 activity requires the presence of the membrane phospholipid phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate [PI(4,5)P2] (Badheka et al., 2015; Tóth et al., 2015), which is a common feature of most TRP channels (Rohacs, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Badheka et al., 2015 and Tóth et al., 2015.

claim: PI(4,5)P2 requirement is a common feature of most TRP channels.
source: We and others have shown recently that in various cellular expression systems PregS-induced TRPM3 activity requires the presence of the membrane phospholipid phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate [PI(4,5)P2] (Badheka et al., 2015; Tóth et al., 2015), which is a common feature of most TRP channels (Rohacs, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Rohacs, 2014.

claim: Stimulation of plasma membrane receptors that induce PI(4,5)P2 hydrolysis via phospholipase C (PLC) activation inhibited heterologously expressed TRPM3 channels.
source: Stimulation of plasma membrane receptors that induce PI(4,5)P2 hydrolysis via phospholipase C (PLC) activation, was shown to inhibit both heterologously expressed TRPM3 channels (Badheka et al., 2015; Tóth et al., 2015) and endogenous TRPM3 in insulinoma cells (Tóth et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Badheka et al., 2015 and Tóth et al., 2015.

claim: Stimulation of plasma membrane receptors that induce PI(4,5)P2 hydrolysis via phospholipase C (PLC) activation inhibited endogenous TRPM3 in insulinoma cells.
source: Stimulation of plasma membrane receptors that induce PI(4,5)P2 hydrolysis via phospholipase C (PLC) activation, was shown to inhibit both heterologously expressed TRPM3 channels (Badheka et al., 2015; Tóth et al., 2015) and endogenous TRPM3 in insulinoma cells (Tóth et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Tóth et al., 2015.

claim: The purified TRPM3 protein in planar lipid bilayers required PI(4,5)P2 for activity induced by PregS.
source: The purified TRPM3 protein in planar lipid bilayers also required PI(4,5)P2 for activity induced by PregS (Uchida et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Uchida et al., 2016.

claim: Nifedipine can induce TRPM3 activity in bilayers in the absence of PI(4,5)P2.
source: Other activators of the channel, nifedipine, or the combination of PregS plus clotrimazole, however, could induce activity in bilayers in the absence of PI(4,5)P2, showing that the requirement for this lipid may be modality dependent (Uchida et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Uchida et al., 2016.

claim: The combination of PregS plus clotrimazole can induce TRPM3 activity in bilayers in the absence of PI(4,5)P2.
source: Other activators of the channel, nifedipine, or the combination of PregS plus clotrimazole, however, could induce activity in bilayers in the absence of PI(4,5)P2, showing that the requirement for this lipid may be modality dependent (Uchida et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Uchida et al., 2016.

claim: The requirement for PI(4,5)P2 in TRPM3 activation may be modality dependent.
source: Other activators of the channel, nifedipine, or the combination of PregS plus clotrimazole, however, could induce activity in bilayers in the absence of PI(4,5)P2, showing that the requirement for this lipid may be modality dependent (Uchida et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Uchida et al., 2016.

claim: Dialysis of PI(4,5)P2 via the patch pipette did not alleviate inhibition of PregS-induced TRPM3 currents by Gq-coupled receptors.
source: Here, we report that dialysis of PI(4,5)P2 via the patch pipette did not alleviate inhibition of PregS-induced TRPM3 currents by Gq-coupled receptors, but co-expression of a protein that binds Gβγ, thus acts as a 'Gβγ sink', significantly attenuated it.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A-C.

claim: Co-expression of a protein that binds Gβγ (a 'Gβγ sink') significantly attenuated inhibition of TRPM3 by Gq-coupled receptors.
source: Here, we report that dialysis of PI(4,5)P2 via the patch pipette did not alleviate inhibition of PregS-induced TRPM3 currents by Gq-coupled receptors, but co-expression of a protein that binds Gβγ, thus acts as a 'Gβγ sink', significantly attenuated it.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D-F.

claim: TRPM3 currents were robustly inhibited by activation of various Gi-coupled receptors.
source: TRPM3 currents were also robustly inhibited by activation of various Gi-coupled receptors, and that effect was also attenuated by Gβγ sinks.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1G-I and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Inhibition of TRPM3 by Gi-coupled receptors was attenuated by Gβγ sinks.
source: TRPM3 currents were also robustly inhibited by activation of various Gi-coupled receptors, and that effect was also attenuated by Gβγ sinks.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1H-I.

claim: Application of purified Gβγ to excised inside-out patches inhibited TRPM3.
source: Application of purified Gβγ to excised inside-out patches inhibited the channel, indicating a direct effect.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A,D.

claim: PregS-induced Ca2+ signals in DRG neurons were inhibited by stimulating Gi-coupled receptors with somatostatin.
source: PregS-induced Ca2+ signals in DRG neurons were inhibited by stimulating Gi-coupled receptors with somatostatin or by the GABAB receptor agonist baclofen.
evidence: This claim is supported by Ca2+ imaging experiments shown in Figure 4B.

claim: PregS-induced Ca2+ signals in DRG neurons were inhibited by the GABAB receptor agonist baclofen.
source: PregS-induced Ca2+ signals in DRG neurons were inhibited by stimulating Gi-coupled receptors with somatostatin or by the GABAB receptor agonist baclofen.
evidence: This claim is supported by Ca2+ imaging experiments shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Baclofen inhibited Ca2+ signals evoked by CIM0216 in DRG neurons.
source: Baclofen also inhibited Ca2+ signals and currents evoked by CIM0216, as well as nocifensive behavioral responses induced by this TRPM3 agonist in vivo.
evidence: This claim is supported by Ca2+ imaging experiments shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Baclofen inhibited currents evoked by CIM0216 in DRG neurons.
source: Baclofen also inhibited Ca2+ signals and currents evoked by CIM0216, as well as nocifensive behavioral responses induced by this TRPM3 agonist in vivo.
evidence: This claim is supported by whole-cell patch clamp experiments shown in Figure 6.

claim: Baclofen inhibited nocifensive behavioral responses induced by CIM0216 in vivo.
source: Baclofen also inhibited Ca2+ signals and currents evoked by CIM0216, as well as nocifensive behavioral responses induced by this TRPM3 agonist in vivo.
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral experiments shown in Figure 7A-B.

claim: TRPM3 is a novel ion channel target of Gβγ subunits.
source: Our data identify TRPM3 as a novel ion channel target of Gβγ subunits.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the multiple lines of experimental evidence presented in the study.

claim: Stimulating M1 muscarinic receptors that couple to PLC inhibited TRPM3.
source: Accordingly, we also found that stimulating M1 muscarinic receptors that couple to PLC inhibited TRPM3; interestingly, this inhibition was faster and more robust than inhibition by the inducible phosphoinositide phosphatases (Badheka et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A and by citation to Badheka et al., 2015.

claim: Inhibition of TRPM3 by M1 muscarinic receptors was faster and more robust than inhibition by inducible phosphoinositide phosphatases.
source: Accordingly, we also found that stimulating M1 muscarinic receptors that couple to PLC inhibited TRPM3; interestingly, this inhibition was faster and more robust than inhibition by the inducible phosphoinositide phosphatases (Badheka et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Badheka et al., 2015.

claim: Carbachol induced fast and complete inhibition of PregS-induced TRPM3 currents in cells expressing M1 muscarinic receptors.
source: Application of 100 μM carbachol induced a fast and complete inhibition.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: In cells dialyzed with 100 μM diC8 PI(4,5)P2, carbachol-induced inhibition of TRPM3 was somewhat smaller, but this difference was not statistically significant (p=0.103).
source: In cells dialyzed with 100 μM diC8 PI(4,5)P2 carbachol-induced inhibition was somewhat smaller, but this difference was not statistically significant (p=0.103) (Figure 1B,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and statistical analysis shown in Figure 1B,C.

claim: Co-expressing the βARK-CT construct significantly attenuated the inhibitory effect of M1 receptor activation by 5 μM Acetylcholine (ACh) on TRPM3.
source: Figure 1D–F shows that co-expressing the βARK-CT construct significantly attenuated the inhibitory effect of M1 receptor activation by 5 μM Acetylcholine (ACh).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D-F.

claim: ACh quickly and completely inhibited PregS-induced TRPM3 currents in cells expressing M2 receptors.
source: Figure 1G shows that ACh quickly and completely inhibited PregS-induced TRPM3 currents in cells expressing M2 receptors.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: Co-expression of βARK-CT significantly attenuated ACh-mediated inhibition of TRPM3 in cells expressing M2 receptors.
source: Figure 1H,I shows that co-expression of βARK-CT significantly attenuated ACh-mediated inhibition.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1H,I.

claim: The inhibitory effect of ACh on TRPM3 was alleviated by the inactivated G203A mutant of the Gαi3 protein.
source: The inhibitory effect of ACh was also alleviated by a different Gβγ sink, the inactivated G203A mutant of the Gαi3 protein (Ogier-Denis et al., 1996) (Figure 1I).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1I and by citation to Ogier-Denis et al., 1996.

claim: Application of carbachol induced a significant decrease in FRET in cells transfected with M1 receptors, indicating a decrease in PI(4,5)P2 levels.
source: Figure 1—figure supplement 1 shows that application of carbachol induced a significant decrease in FRET in cells transfected with M1 receptors, indicating a decrease in PI(4,5)P2 levels, whereas in cells transfected with M2 receptors, PI(4,5)P2 levels did not change.
evidence: This claim is supported by FRET measurements shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: In cells transfected with M2 receptors, PI(4,5)P2 levels did not change upon carbachol application.
source: Figure 1—figure supplement 1 shows that application of carbachol induced a significant decrease in FRET in cells transfected with M1 receptors, indicating a decrease in PI(4,5)P2 levels, whereas in cells transfected with M2 receptors, PI(4,5)P2 levels did not change.
evidence: This claim is supported by FRET measurements shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Overexpressed M2 receptors do not signal to PLC.
source: These data show that overexpressed M2 receptors do not signal to PLC and that endogenous Gq-coupled muscarinic receptors in HEK cells do not express at sufficiently high levels to induce a significant decrease in PI(4,5)P2 levels.
evidence: This is inferred from the FRET measurements showing no change in PI(4,5)P2 levels upon M2 receptor activation.

claim: Endogenous Gq-coupled muscarinic receptors in HEK cells do not express at sufficiently high levels to induce a significant decrease in PI(4,5)P2 levels.
source: These data show that overexpressed M2 receptors do not signal to PLC and that endogenous Gq-coupled muscarinic receptors in HEK cells do not express at sufficiently high levels to induce a significant decrease in PI(4,5)P2 levels.
evidence: This is inferred from the FRET measurements showing no change in PI(4,5)P2 levels upon M2 receptor activation.

claim: PLC activation is not necessary for inhibition of TRPM3 upon GPCR activation.
source: These results show that PLC activation is not necessary for inhibition of TRPM3 upon GPCR activation.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that M2 receptors inhibit TRPM3 without activating PLC.

claim: The inhibitory effect of muscarinic M1 or M2 receptor activation on TRPM3 did not depend on the presence of extracellular Ca2+.
source: The inhibitory effect of muscarinic M1 or M2 receptor activation on TRPM3 did not depend on the presence of extracellular Ca2+, as ACh and carbachol inhibited PregS-induced TRPM3 currents in the absence of extracellular Ca2+ (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A,B.

claim: TRPM3 channels have an alternative permeation pathway that is open when clotrimazole and PregS are co-applied.
source: TRPM3 channels have an alternative permeation pathway that is open when clotrimazole and PregS are co-applied (Vriens et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Vriens et al., 2014.

claim: The alternative permeation pathway of TRPM3 displays lower level of inward rectification, and thus higher current levels at negative voltages.
source: This alternative pathway displays lower level of inward rectification, and thus higher current levels at negative voltages.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the alternative permeation pathway of TRPM3.

claim: Currents induced by clotrimazole/PregS were fully inhibited by ACh in cells expressing M2 receptors.
source: Figure 1—figure supplement 2C shows that currents induced by clotrimazole/PregS were also fully inhibited by ACh.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Application of quinpirole to cells expressing D2 and TRPM3 resulted in complete inhibition of TRPM3 currents induced by PregS.
source: Figure 1—figure supplement 2D shows that application of quinpirole to cells expressing D2 and TRPM3 resulted in complete inhibition of TRPM3 currents induced by either PregS, or the combination of PregS and clotrimazole.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2D.

claim: Application of quinpirole to cells expressing D2 and TRPM3 resulted in complete inhibition of TRPM3 currents induced by the combination of PregS and clotrimazole.
source: Figure 1—figure supplement 2D shows that application of quinpirole to cells expressing D2 and TRPM3 resulted in complete inhibition of TRPM3 currents induced by either PregS, or the combination of PregS and clotrimazole.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2D.

claim: Activation of the Gi-coupled M2 muscarinic receptors inhibit TRPM3 currents under a variety of experimental conditions and channel activation modalities.
source: Overall, these data show that activation of the Gi-coupled M2 muscarinic, or D2 dopamine receptors inhibit TRPM3 currents under a variety of experimental conditions and channel activation modalities.
evidence: This is a summary statement supported by the data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Activation of the Gi-coupled D2 dopamine receptors inhibit TRPM3 currents under a variety of experimental conditions and channel activation modalities.
source: Overall, these data show that activation of the Gi-coupled M2 muscarinic, or D2 dopamine receptors inhibit TRPM3 currents under a variety of experimental conditions and channel activation modalities.
evidence: This is a summary statement supported by the data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: G-protein βγ subunits play an important role in TRPM3 current inhibition upon M1 muscarinic receptor activation.
source: Our data so far suggest that G-protein βγ subunits play an important role in TRPM3 current inhibition upon M1 muscarinic receptor activation.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing that Gβγ sinks attenuate inhibition by M1 receptor activation.

claim: PDGF inhibited PregS-induced currents in Xenopus oocytes co-expressing TRPM3 and PDGFRβ.
source: Figure 1—figure supplement 3 shows that PDGF inhibited PregS-induced currents in Xenopus oocytes co-expressing TRPM3 and PDGFRβ, but not in cells expressing the Y1009F Y1021F mutant.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: PDGF did not inhibit PregS-induced currents in Xenopus oocytes co-expressing TRPM3 and the Y1009F-Y1021F mutant of PDGFRβ.
source: Figure 1—figure supplement 3 shows that PDGF inhibited PregS-induced currents in Xenopus oocytes co-expressing TRPM3 and PDGFRβ, but not in cells expressing the Y1009F Y1021F mutant.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: PLC activation is sufficient to inhibit TRPM3 activity in the absence of G-protein activation.
source: These data show that in principle, PLC activation is sufficient to inhibit TRPM3 activity in the absence of G-protein activation.
evidence: This is inferred from the PDGFR experiments showing inhibition without G-protein activation.

claim: Co-expression of Gβ1γ2 significantly inhibited TRPM3 currents in Xenopus oocytes.
source: Co-expression of Gβ1γ2 significantly inhibited TRPM3 currents (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A-C.

claim: Wild type Gαi3 did not inhibit PregS-induced TRPM3 activity in Xenopus oocytes.
source: Neither the wild type nor the constitutively active mutant Gα subunits inhibited PregS-induced TRPM3 activity (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The constitutively active G205L mutant of Gαi2 did not inhibit PregS-induced TRPM3 activity in Xenopus oocytes.
source: Neither the wild type nor the constitutively active mutant Gα subunits inhibited PregS-induced TRPM3 activity (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The constitutively active G205L mutant of Gαo did not inhibit PregS-induced TRPM3 activity in Xenopus oocytes.
source: Neither the wild type nor the constitutively active mutant Gα subunits inhibited PregS-induced TRPM3 activity (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Gβγ, but not Gα subunits inhibit TRPM3 channels.
source: These data indicate that Gβγ, but not Gα subunits inhibit TRPM3 channels.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Gβ5 does not potentiate GIRK channels.
source: We also tested the effect of Gβ5, a subunit, which does not potentiate GIRK channels (Mirshahi et al., 2002), and found that it had no inhibitory effect on TRPM3 when co-expressed with Gγ2 (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Mirshahi et al., 2002.

claim: Gβ5 had no inhibitory effect on TRPM3 when co-expressed with Gγ2.
source: We also tested the effect of Gβ5, a subunit, which does not potentiate GIRK channels (Mirshahi et al., 2002), and found that it had no inhibitory effect on TRPM3 when co-expressed with Gγ2 (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: TRPM3 currents displayed a substantial rundown in excised patches, after a transient initial increase upon patch excision.
source: Consistent with earlier results (Badheka et al., 2015), TRPM3 currents displayed a substantial rundown in excised patches, after a transient initial increase upon patch excision (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A,B and by citation to Badheka et al., 2015.

claim: Current rundown of TRPM3 in excised patches is caused by the decrease of endogenous PI(4,5)P2 levels in the patch membrane.
source: We showed earlier that this current rundown is caused by the decrease of endogenous PI(4,5)P2 levels in the patch membrane (Badheka et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Badheka et al., 2015.

claim: TRPM3 channel activity was restored by the application of diC8 PI(4,5)P2 in excised patches.
source: Accordingly, channel activity was restored by the application of diC8 PI(4,5)P2, and when purified recombinant Gβ1γ2 (50 ng/ml) was applied to the patch in the continued presence of PI(4,5)P2, currents were inhibited (Figure 3A,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Purified recombinant Gβ1γ2 (50 ng/ml) applied to excised patches in the continued presence of PI(4,5)P2 inhibited TRPM3 currents.
source: Accordingly, channel activity was restored by the application of diC8 PI(4,5)P2, and when purified recombinant Gβ1γ2 (50 ng/ml) was applied to the patch in the continued presence of PI(4,5)P2, currents were inhibited (Figure 3A,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A,D.

claim: The inhibition of TRPM3 by Gβγ in excised patches developed slowly, but it was almost complete in most patches.
source: The inhibition developed slowly, but it was almost complete in most patches.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental observations shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Boiled Gβγ applied in the same protocol had no inhibitory effect on TRPM3 in excised patches.
source: Boiled Gβγ applied in the same protocol had no inhibitory effect (Figure 3B,D), and purified Gαi1 did not inhibit channel activity either (Figure 3C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B,D.

claim: Purified Gαi1 did not inhibit TRPM3 channel activity in excised patches.
